author: haiku
label: climb-02-01
changes: Removed the CheckoutFailed event and the Cart reactions to it (Q4). Nothing published it, and Cart changes only on OrderConfirmed.
Added a table of how each link works, HTTP or broker event (Q3).
Place order now returns once the order is PLACED, and the customer's page polls Order for status (Q1).
Cart sends cart id, lines and unit prices in the POST /orders body (Q1).
Payment replies 202 once the provider accepts the charge, and Order retries POST /charges with the same key (Q2).
Claim now fails with 409 when the hold is not HELD or expires_at has passed. A claim already made by the same order returns 200. Order acknowledges PaymentSucceeded only after a 200 or 409 (Q6).
Release on an EXPIRED reservation is a no-op (Q7).
Refund outcome now arrives by webhook, with a PaymentRefunded event that Order uses to send the refund email (Q5).
Removed the REFUND_STUCK order status. A stuck refund is an ops alert on the refund row in Payment, and retries continue.
Merged the duplicate webhook rules and the stores table into one place, and merged the design-in-brief bullets that repeated the flowchart.
Moved the first-outcome-wins rule into Decisions, with the first-outcome reasoning from Q8.
Design in brief: added an Outbox bullet explaining the term and why events can repeat (Q9).
Design in brief: added a bullet that every call and event can arrive twice and each receiver ignores repeats (Q9, Q13).
Order statuses: added the rule for when the customer's page stops polling and what PAYMENT_PENDING shows (Q15).
How the services talk: Order to Inventory rows say each call is keyed by order id; PaymentRefundRequired carries order id and full amount (Q10, Q14).
Flowchart RESERVE node: added that the call is retried with the same order id until a reply (Q10).
Flowchart PAYREQ node: Order saves PAYMENT_PENDING before POST /charges (Q12).
Flowchart CHARGE node: Payment stores the provider charge id on accept (Q11).
Flowchart webhook and APPLY nodes: the webhook carries provider event id and provider charge id, and Payment finds the charge by provider charge id (Q11).
Flowchart CONF node: confirmation email is written in the same transaction as CONFIRMED (Q13).
Flowchart LATE/REFREQ and REFUND nodes: refund amount is the full amount, and Payment finds the charge by order id (Q14).
Flowchart refund webhook node: names provider event id and refund id (Q11).
What each service stores: refunds gained provider refund id; Payment and Order both gained an outbox table (Q9, Q11).
Failure branches: added a reserve-reply-lost row (Q10).
Open questions: merged the charge-never-accepted question into one calls-that-never-get-a-reply question covering reserve and charge (Q10).
Merged the "Design in brief" bullets into a short Overview. Removed the bullets that repeated the flowchart's steps, and merged the outbox explanation into one bullet.
Merged the "How the services talk" table and the "What each service stores" table into one Services table, so each service's storage and its calls and events sit in one row.

Shortened flowchart node labels by removing repeated wording (for example, "Stores:" lines that restated the Services table only where needed, and duplicate "Customer sees" wording). Kept every node, branch and failure path from the original, including the expiry job, the 202/503 charge replies, the webhook dedup checks, and the refund retry loop.
Merged the two webhook dedup descriptions (charge and refund) into the flowchart's own nodes and the Failure branches table, rather than repeating them in prose.
Shortened the status polling rule to one sentence and removed the repeated statement of when the page stops polling.
Kept Decisions 1 to 3 and the four Open questions unchanged in substance; Open questions remain grouped at the end. No plan behaviour was changed.
